host_shaped_import_check_notes.first_two_runs_were_my_instrument_not_th: Run 1 used python -I and read 5 of 6: app.tools failed ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'anyio', because -I ignores the user site-packages that carries it. That is a DEPENDENCY absence, not a depth failure, and the host runs under its own venv with every dep -- so -I was dropped and the check read 6 of 6. Run 2 then read trading_days_behind_t1 = null with 'the trading calendar cannot place ... (ValueError)' for every probe, which LOOKED like a regression against v2's measured 2. It was my stamp SHAPE: _behind parses %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ -- a LITERAL Z, which is what S3 LastModified renders -- and I passed +00:00. The corrected probes read 3, 1 and 0 trading days behind T-1 for 2026-10-09, 10-13 and 10-14, and the wrong-shape probe is KEPT as a control that comes back ABSENT, so the record can tell a wrong instrument from a real defect. v2's 2 against today's 3 for the same 2026-10-09 stamp is one trading day of clock movement: T-1 was 2026-10-13 then and reads 2026-10-14 now.

blocking_for_phase_b.what: deploying from THIS tree moves the /yearinreview page's served md5 from 0d828b51 to 3bbd5ab2 -- identical content, 344 line terminators. The path carries .gitattributes eol=lf, so the blob is LF and every clean checkout materialises LF; yr-1 shipped from a tree whose WORKING COPY held the CRO's CRLF bytes, and the deploy tars the working copy. git reports the path CLEAN in both trees because eol=lf normalises on read. A later yr1.AC2 run would then read host-md5 != source and FAIL against a correct deploy. Two routes in the row; the issuer rules before Phase B.
